items.problem: Nullable-reference warnings (CS8618/CS8600/CS8601/CS8602/CS8604/CS8625) emitted from ported UWP code under the scaffold's <Nullable>enable</Nullable>.
items.evidence: build-output.txt: 14x CS8618, 8x CS8600, etc. Build still succeeded ('The build succeeds with 0 errors (only warnings)').
items.covered_clearly_at: N/A — these are non-blocking warnings inherent to enabling nullable on legacy code; not a fidelity or build defect and not a skill topic.
items.why_no_skill_change: Warnings did not affect build success, runtime, or parity (100/100). Suppressing/annotating nullable on ported code is generic C# hygiene, not UWP->WinUI-specific guidance; a re-run would still pass regardless. Adding skill prose about it would be noise.
